outcomeNote: An editorial note identifying whom the mishna does not follow

segments.he: לֹא הֵסִיר אֶת הַמּוּרְאָה כּוּ׳. מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן; דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן: שָׁמַעְתִּי שֶׁמַּבְדִּילִין בְּחַטַּאת הָעוֹף.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that if the priest «did not remove the crop,» or he changed any detail of the sacrificial rite after he squeezed out the blood, the offering is valid. If he separated the head from the body of a bird sin offering, it is disqualified. The Gemara says: «The mishna is not in accordance with» the opinion of «Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, as it is taught» in a baraita that «Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Shimon, said: I heard that one may separate» the head from the body «of a bird sin offering.»
